docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome, and they are greatly appreciated! Every little bit helps, and credit will always be given.

docs.title: Areas for contribution
docs.text: The project follows a modular approach to make it easier to support new RTL Generators and Testcases.

docs.title: Adding support for a new RTL Coding style.
docs.text:
There are dozens of proprietary and opensource tools for generating RTL code from IP-XACT, SystemRDL, CSV or other inhouse formats. These tools will define their fields in a fixed pattern, e.g. <prefix>_<RegisterName>_<signalName> or <signalName> or ...

To add support to a particular style of signal naming,

  1. create a new file under src/cocotbext/i2s/callbacks/bsv.py
    1. Preferably name the file as .py
    2. define your class and define the read and write functions in it.
    3. submit a PR.

docs.title: Adding support for a new TestCases.
docs.text: The current version of i2s supports reset check and simple rw_test with foreground and background read/write combinations. There are a bunch of additional tests that are normally written for checking registers. To contribute a new test: 1. Add your test to src/cocotbext/i2s/testcases folder 2. Submit a PR.

docs.title: Environment setup
docs.text:
Nothing easier!

Fork and clone the repository, then:

cd cocotbext/i2s
pdm install

NOTE: If it fails for some reason, you'll need to install PDM manually.

You can install it with:

python3 -m pip install --user pipx
pipx install pdm

Now you can try running pdm install.

You now have the dependencies installed.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
This project uses duty to run tasks. A Makefile is also provided. The Makefile will try to run certain tasks on multiple Python versions. If for some reason you don't want to run the task on multiple Python versions, you run the task directly with pdm run duty TASK.

The Makefile detects if a virtual environment is activated, so make will work the same with the virtualenv activated or not.

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
As usual:

  1. create a new branch: git switch -c feature-or-bugfix-name
  2. edit the code and/or the documentation

Before committing:

  1. run pdm run duty format to auto-format the code
  2. run pdm run duty check to check everything (fix any warning)
  3. run make C tests to run the tests (fix any issue)
  4. if you updated the documentation or the project dependencies:
    1. run pdm run duty docs
    2. go to http://localhost:8000 and check that everything looks good
  5. follow our commit message convention

If you are unsure about how to fix or ignore a warning, just let the continuous integration fail, and we will help you during review.

Don't bother updating the changelog, we will take care of this.

docs.title: Commit message convention
docs.text:
Commit messages must follow our convention based on the Angular style or the Karma convention:

<type>[(scope)]: Subject

[Body]

Subject and body must be valid Markdown. Subject must have proper casing (uppercase for first letter if it makes sense), but no dot at the end, and no punctuation in general.

Scope and body are optional. Type can be:

  • build: About packaging, building wheels, etc.
  • chore: About packaging or repo/files management.
  • ci: About Continuous Integration.
  • deps: Dependencies update.
  • docs: About documentation.
  • feat: New feature.
  • fix: Bug fix.
  • perf: About performance.
  • refactor: Changes that are not features or bug fixes.
  • style: A change in code style/format.
  • tests: About tests.

If you write a body, please add trailers at the end (for example issues and PR references, or co-authors), without relying on GitHub's flavored Markdown:

Body.

Issue #10: https://github.com/namespace/project/issues/10
Related to PR namespace/other-project#15: https://github.com/namespace/other-project/pull/15

These "trailers" must appear at the end of the body, without any blank lines between them. The trailer title can contain any character except colons :. We expect a full URI for each trailer, not just GitHub autolinks (for example, full GitHub URLs for commits and issues, not the hash or the #issue-number).

We do not enforce a line length on commit messages summary and body, but please avoid very long summaries, and very long lines in the body, unless they are part of code blocks that must not be wrapped.

docs.title: Pull requests guidelines
docs.text:
Link to any related issue in the Pull Request message.

During the review, we recommend using fixups:

# SHA is the SHA of the commit you want to fix
git commit --fixup=SHA

Once all the changes are approved, you can squash your commits:

git rebase -i --autosquash main

And force-push:

git push -f

If this seems all too complicated, you can push or force-push each new commit, and we will squash them ourselves if needed, before merging.

docs.title: i2s
docs.text:
I2S cocotb extension package.

This package provides I2S (Inter-IC Sound) bus models, drivers, and configuration utilities for use with cocotb-based testbenches.

Modules:

  • bus –

    I2S bus definition for cocotb.

  • config –

    Configuration utilities for the I2S driver.

  • driver –

    I2S driver implementation for cocotb.

Classes:

  • I2sBus –

    Abstraction of the I2S bus for cocotb.

  • I2sConfig –

    I2S configuration container.

  • I2sDriver –

    Driver for interacting with an I2S bus in cocotb testbenches.

docs.title: I2sBus
docs.text:
I2sBus(dut: SimHandleBase, name: str = 'i2s')

Abstraction of the I2S bus for cocotb.

Parameters:

  • dut (SimHandleBase) –

    The device under test handle from cocotb.

  • name (str, default: 'i2s' ) –

    Name of the bus instance. Defaults to "i2s".

Source code in src/cocotbext/i2s/bus.py 
def __init__(self, dut: SimHandleBase, name: str = "i2s") -> None:
    """Initialize the I2S bus.

    Args:
        dut (SimHandleBase): The device under test handle from cocotb.
        name (str, optional): Name of the bus instance. Defaults to "i2s".
    """
    self.dut = dut
    self.name = name

    # Example: attach bus signals if they exist
    self.sck = getattr(dut, f"{name}_sck", None)
    self.ws = getattr(dut, f"{name}_ws", None)
    self.sd = getattr(dut, f"{name}_sd", None)

  • name (str, default: None ) –

    Optional driver name. Defaults to None.

Methods:

    Register a callback into the scoreboard.

  • read –

    Read data from a given address over the I2S bus.

  • write –

    Write data to a given address over the I2S bus.

Source code in src/cocotbext/i2s/driver.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    bus: I2sBus,
    config: I2sConfig = default_config,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize the I2S driver.

    Args:
        bus: I2S bus instance.
        config (I2sConfig, optional): Configuration object for the bus.
            Defaults to `default_config`.
        name (str, optional): Optional driver name. Defaults to None.
    """
    self.bus = bus
    self.config = config
    self.name = name

def __init__(self, dut: SimHandleBase, name: str = "i2s") -> None:
    """Initialize the I2S bus.

    Args:
        dut (SimHandleBase): The device under test handle from cocotb.
        name (str, optional): Name of the bus instance. Defaults to "i2s".
    """
    self.dut = dut
    self.name = name

    # Example: attach bus signals if they exist
    self.sck = getattr(dut, f"{name}_sck", None)
    self.ws = getattr(dut, f"{name}_ws", None)
    self.sd = getattr(dut, f"{name}_sd", None)

def __init__(
    self,
    bus: I2sBus,
    config: I2sConfig = default_config,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize the I2S driver.

    Args:
        bus: I2S bus instance.
        config (I2sConfig, optional): Configuration object for the bus.
            Defaults to `default_config`.
        name (str, optional): Optional driver name. Defaults to None.
    """
    self.bus = bus
    self.config = config
    self.name = name
